newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: RTRS-Chan says loan to help PNG cut interest rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Chan says loan to help PNG cut interest rates.

text.p: Papua New Guinea prime minister Sir Julius Chan said on Wednesday the release of the second tranche of a World Bank/International Monetary Fund loan would help bring lower interest rates.
The World Bank approved the release of the second US$25 million tranche of the US$50 million economic recovery programme loan earlier this month.
Chan said in a statement the second tranche funds would be fully drawn down during the 1997 calendar year.
"In addition to easing the demands on the Treasury coffers, the loan will allow the government to substitute domestic financing with foreign concessional finance," Chan said.
"This will aid the government's efforts to mobilise domestic resources by lowering interest rates," he said.
"By lowering interest rates, we will see the current trend of economic recovery in all sectors of the community sustained throughout 1997 and well into 1998," he said.
Chan released the statement after meeting Richard Calkins, head of the PNG and Pacific Islands division of the World Bank.
